Ok this is kinda crazy. 

You’ve probably heard that you should walk 10,000 steps a day.

But did you know this is not a real target set by medical professionals?

It all started because of a marketing campaign. 

Back in 1964 a Japanese company wanted to increase sales of their pedometer, which is a device to count how many steps you take.

And what better way to do that, than tell everyone they need to walk 10k steps every day. 

But they only chose that number because the Japanese character for 10,000 (万) kinda looks like a person walking...

So next time you hear you’re meant to walk 10,000 steps a day, remember it’s all because a  Japanese company wanted to sell more of their product.

SONY DOCUMENTARY - If you wanted to start a business, Japan after World War Two was probably the worst place for that…  However, inside a bomb-damaged office building in the middle of Tokyo, two engineers began their dream company against all odds. And fast forward to today, SONY is everywhere. From consumer electronics, to music, movies, video games, and even an entire line of robot dogs… SONY does it all. But with their hands in so many industries, they’re faced with the brutal reality about business: Enemies are everywhere. Throughout their history, SONY has faced many battles - including being stabbed in the back by Nintendo, and potentially infiltrated by the North Korean government. So in this video, we’re unraveling the entire history of SONY… Their rise from a struggling radio-repair service to a $100 billion empire. Welcome to the true story of SONY - covering the rise of SONY and Sony's history from humble beginnings to tech giant. For more business stories and business documentaries, subscribe to MagnatesMedia! I hope you enjoy learning about the rise of Sony. :)

How did Sony get so big? How did Sony become successful? To understand that, let's see the story of Sony's founders... Akio Morita was born in Japan in 1921. For the past 14 generations, his family had run a brewery that had passed down from father to son. Even from just 10 years old, Akio was attending all the company’s board meetings. However, he seemed more interested in tinkering with radios and phonographs than running the family business. And he begged his father to let him study physics and engineering instead of economics. After Japan bombed Pearl Harbor, the army drafted millions of military-aged men - but since Akio studied physics, he could design weapons for the army instead of fighting on the front lines. So in 1944, Akio got an engineering job in the navy. And that’s where he met his future business partner: Masaru Ibuka. This is the duo that would start SONY, a business that would span so many different industries. #business #sony #documentary #company #story #entertainment #tech #businesssuccess

Fanta has a dark origin story, as the drink was initially made from food scraps in Nazi Germany.

It all began when Japan bombed pearl harbour and america entered world war II, as this meant American companies had to stop doing business with Germany. 

This was a disaster for Max Keith, who was the head of Coca-Cola in Germany.

Suddenly he could no longer import Coke syrup from America, and so he had no product to sell. 

But Keith wasn’t gonna give up that easily.

He ordered a team of chemists to create a new drink for the German market that was kind of similar to coke - it would still be a fizzy caffeinated soft drink, but since they couldn’t use coke syrup, they used leftovers like apple fibers, fruit pulp, and whey, which is the byproduct of cheese curdling. 

It doesn’t exactly sound appealing. 

But they branded the new drink Fanta, and it became a huge hit in Germany. Especially since many foreign soft drinks had been banned due to the war.

After Hitler was defeated, the Coca-Cola company rebranded Fanta and changed the recipe to get away from its Nazi past. 

They also promoted Keith, who helped make Fanta one of biggest soft drinks in the world.
